content: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 RETR: Customer Support Specialist Anywhere in the World 🇺🇸 United States of America Virginia Customer Support Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/5755/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://retr.app/">https://retr.app/</a> </p> <h2>Why this role matters now</h2> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">A loan officer's business runs on relationships. Ours runs on making sure RETR never gets in the way of theirs.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">When something breaks for a customer, a real deal is on the line, and what they need is a person who understands both the product and their business. That person is you.</p> <p class="font-claude-response-body break-words whitespace-normal">Most support jobs are a treadmill: you answer the question, the question comes back, you answer it again. Here the work compounds. A good answer becomes an article, the article teaches our AI, and the question stops coming. We measure which articles resolve and which fail, so you can watch the queue shrink because of something you wrote.</p> <h2>What you'll do</h2> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Be the first human a customer talks to, across email, chat, and phone, for individual and enterprise accounts alike</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Answer the hard half. Our AI handles the routine questions; what reaches you is the ambiguous, the technical, and the high-stakes</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Write and improve the knowledge base articles that make the AI better and the queue smaller. We measure which articles resolve and which fail, and we fix the ones that fail</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Build real fluency in mortgage and real estate workflows, deep enough to explain our product in the customer's language rather than ours</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Take actions that carry weight: refunds, cancellations, and billing corrections in Stripe</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Surface product friction to Engineering with enough evidence that it gets fixed, then tell the customer when it ships</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Hand inbound leads to Sales cleanly. Support does not sell, but Support is often the first to touch a future enterprise deal</p> <h2>The first 90 days</h2> <p class="MsoNormal">Two things in this job reach customers at scale without a human in between: the knowledge base, which feeds our AI, and our enterprise accounts. A knowledge base article that is 80 percent right makes the AI wrong for everyone who asks. So neither one is handed to you on a calendar date. Both are handed over when you have earned them.</p> <p class="MsoNormal"><strong>Days 1 to 14. </strong>Product and customer mastery. Learn what every search does and why a customer would use it. Read every knowledge source we have. Study the queue, open and closed. Start answering emails and chats.</p> <p class="MsoNormal"><strong>Days 15 to 30. </strong>Triage with ease. Route what you cannot answer to the right place. Start taking phone calls, which demand faster answers than anything written.</p> <p class="MsoNormal"><strong>Day 30. </strong>You can run the inbox alone, handle refunds and cancellations, and walk a customer through troubleshooting without help. You will run a mock demo of the platform with your manager playing the customer.</p> <p class="MsoNormal"><strong>Day 60. </strong>You start owning knowledge base articles. If a customer asks something twice, you write it.</p> <p class="MsoNormal"><strong>Day 90. </strong>Full coverage, including enterprise, to the white-glove standard those customers expect. The test that matters: your manager can be offline for a week and nothing breaks.</p> <p class="MsoNormal">We would rather ramp you properly than throw you at enterprise in week three and apologize to a customer for it.</p> <h2>The team</h2> <p class="MsoNormal">Two people. You report to our Customer Support Manager. She reports to our COO. That is the org.</p> <p class="MsoNormal">You will also work directly with Engineering on bugs and escalations, with Customer Enablement on onboarding, and with Sales on inbound leads. We are twelve people. Everyone reaches across.</p> <h2>The stack</h2> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><strong>Support. </strong>HubSpot for tickets, SLAs, and reporting. Aircall for phone. Stripe for billing.</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><strong>AI. </strong>An AI agent handling first-line resolution, tuned against a knowledge base you will help own.</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span><strong>Product. </strong>The RETR platform: search, lists, exports, alerts, and enterprise account management.</p> <h2>What we're looking for</h2> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>1 to 3 years in a customer-facing role, ideally at a B2B SaaS company</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Genuine patience and real critical thinking. Most of what reaches you will not have an obvious answer</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>You explain the why behind an issue rather than just the fix, because that is what builds trust</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>Sharp attention to detail in how you document requests, troubleshooting steps, and interactions, plus the instinct to see a problem before it lands</p> <p class="MsoListParagraph"><span><span>•<span>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span></span>You would rather fix the root cause than close the ticket</p> <p class="MsoListPara
